Answer all questions.  For each question there are four possible answers A, B, C and D. Choose the one you consider correct and record your choice in soft pencil on the multiple choice answer sheet.  Follow the instructions on the multiple choice answer sheet.  Write in soft pencil.  Write your name, centre number and candidate number on the multiple choice answer sheet in the spaces provided unless this has been done for you.  Do not use correction fluid.  Do not write on any bar codes.  You may use a calculator. INFORMATION  The total mark for this paper is 30.  Each correct answer will score one mark.  Any rough working should be done on this question paper.
During a period of deflation an economy’s aggregate monetary demand falls. Which function of money explains this fall?

options.B: a medium of exchange
options.D: a store of value

options.B: no yes yes

options.B: decreases increases
options.D: increases increases

questions.questionText: A government wishes to ensure adequate flood defences are provided in its coastal areas. Which action is most likely to be undertaken only by the government?

options.B: designing the defences
options.D: maintaining the defences

questions.questionText: Consumer surplus exists in the market for rice. What does this mean?

options.A: Consumers benefit from rice production more than producers.
options.B: Consumer demand for rice exceeds supply.
options.C: Some consumers would be willing to pay more than the market price for rice.
options.D: The production of rice exceeds the supply.

questions.questionText: The diagram shows the demand curve and supply curve for a product. S X price Y W D O Z quantity Which area represents producer surplus?

options.B: OWYZ minus OYZ
options.D: OXYZ minus WXY

questions.questionText: The diagram shows the relationship between total expenditure and price for three products, 1, 2 and 3. price O total expenditure Which curves represent the products with price-elastic and unitary price-elastic demand? elastic unitary
What causes an inelastic market supply curve for an agricultural crop such as wheat?

options.A: a government decision to import crops at times of shortage
options.B: an efficient use of fertilisers causing crop production to rise
options.C: the storage of excess production for future sale
options.D: the very long time required to produce additional output

options.D: Y is a derived demand from X.

The market for a product is initially in equilibrium. Which combination of changes will cause the price of the product to rise and the quantity sold to fall?

options.A: a decrease in demand that is larger than a decrease in supply
options.B: a decrease in demand that is smaller than a decrease in supply
options.C: an increase in demand that is larger than an increase in supply
options.D: an increase in demand that is smaller than an increase in supply

questions.questionText: The diagram shows two demand curves and two supply curves. The initial equilibrium is at H. price H K O quantity Which combinations of shifts in the demand and supply curves would result in a change in the equilibrium position from H to K?

options.A: an increase in demand and an increase in supply
options.B: an increase in demand and a decrease in supply
options.C: a decrease in demand and an increase in supply
options.D: a decrease in demand and a decrease in supply

questions.questionText: In 2009, the Australian Government made a payment of $900 to those who earned less than $100000 per year. How would this payment best be described?

options.B: progressive
options.D: regressive

questions.questionText: The market for good Z is in equilibrium with 1000 units sold at a price of $10. The government pays a subsidy of $2 per unit to producers of good Z. Under which conditions will the total spending by the government on the subsidy be smallest? price elasticity of price elasticity of demand for good Z supply for good Z
If an industry is currently state-owned and state-run, what does not represent a reason for it being privatised?

options.A: Decisions will no longer be taken with political considerations in mind.
options.B: The benefits of merit goods will be taken into account in decision-making.
options.C: Its owners would have more incentive to make it operate profitably.
options.D: There will be greater incentives for managers to introduce modern technology.

questions.questionText: What does the incidence of an indirect tax on a product refer to?

options.A: the proportion of the tax paid by the consumer relative to the producer
options.B: the reduction in output as a result of the imposition of the tax
options.C: the revenue the tax generates for the government
options.D: the increase in the hidden economy as a result of tax evasion after the tax is imposed

questions.questionText: A government wishes to influence the price of a good. It introduces a maximum price, P , and a max minimum price, P . min The diagram shows these prices relative to the current market price P. S price P P max P min D O quantity What can be concluded from the diagram?

options.A: Both the maximum and the minimum price will be effective.
options.B: Only the maximum price will be effective.
options.C: Only the minimum price will be effective.
options.D: The market price will continue to operate.

questions.questionText: An economy is initially in equilibrium. Which combination of events will definitely cause an increase in the general price level of the economy and a decrease in its real output? aggregate short-run demand aggregate supply

options.B: decreases unchanged
options.D: unchanged decreases

questions.questionText: The government of a country changes from a balanced budget to a budget deficit. From which point along the country’s long-run aggregate supply curve (LRAS) will this change cause the largest increase in employment without creating inflationary pressure? LRAS price level D C

options.A: downward shift of the aggregate demand curve

questions.questionText: Trade in services is a component of the current account of the balance of payments. What is an example of a trade in services?

options.B: export revenue from primary commodities
options.D: income from overseas investments

questions.questionText: Which statement about changing price levels is correct?

options.A: Anyone on a fixed income has rising real income during deflation.
options.B: Government revenue from indirect taxes falls during inflation.
options.D: Savers prefer index-linked savings when there is deflation rather than inflation.

questions.questionText: What would be likely to decrease inflation in an economy?

options.B: a decrease in unemployment
options.D: an increase in taxes on imports

questions.questionText: Which change in economic circumstances is most likely to lead to a reduction in the rate of domestic inflation in an economy?

options.B: a reduction in the productivity of labour
options.D: an increase in direct taxes to finance increased welfare payments

questions.questionText: A country is currently experiencing deflation. It has a large national debt that is greater than its annual real income. Which combination of policies is most likely to increase the general price level without adding to the national debt? fiscal policy monetary policy

options.A: decrease the budget deficit decrease the money supply
options.B: decrease the budget deficit increase the money supply
options.C: increase the budget deficit decrease the money supply
options.D: increase the budget deficit increase the money supply
